content.text:
I submitted **index 26 (Sb fraction 0.889)** as the best composition. It gave 0.127% EQE, about 10× better than anything else I measured.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.312 | 0.0030 |
| 12 | 0.558 | 0.0034 |
| 16 | 0.687 | 0.0035 |
| 22 | 0.829 | 0.0124 |
| **26** | **0.889** | **0.1271** |

- **Flat middle:** EQE stayed at about 0.003% from Sb 0.31 to 0.69. That range spans the Cu₂SbO₅ (Sb ≈ 0.33) and CuSb₂O₆ (Sb ≈ 0.667) compositions. I checked those first because CuSb₂O₆ is a known photoanode material, but they weren't the best here.
- **Sb-rich end:** EQE rose sharply past Sb 0.8. The Gaussian-process model then pointed to the Sb-rich end, and index 26 was the best point.

**What's uncertain:**
- EQE was still climbing at index 26. The true best composition could be index 27 or 28 (Sb 0.90), which I couldn't measure because all 5 EQE measurements were used.
- I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phases are unconfirmed. My guess that the Sb-rich films are CuSb₂O₆ mixed with antimony oxide rests on composition alone.
